instruction: In networkx, reading a graph's cached views (G.edges and G.degree, and in_edges, out_edges, in_degree and out_degree on directed graphs) stores a view on the graph that refers back to the graph, so any graph whose views were read is part of a reference cycle and is freed only by the cyclic garbage collector. Make such a graph freed by reference counting alone: with gc disabled, a Graph, DiGraph, MultiGraph or MultiDiGraph with some edges, on which nodes, adj, edges, in_edges, out_edges, degree, in_degree and out_degree were read (where they exist) and number_of_edges() and str() were called, is gone as soon as its last reference is deleted (a weakref.ref to it returns None). Views must keep working when their graph was only a temporary, for all four graph classes: with edges = [(0, 1), (1, 2)] and G = Graph(edges), dict(Graph(edges).degree(weight='w')), dict(Graph(edges).degree([1])), Graph(edges).degree(1, weight='w'), list(Graph(edges).edges([1])) and list(Graph(edges).edges(data=True, nbunch=[1])) equal the same calls on G, and so do views of G.copy() and G.subgraph(...). After copy.deepcopy or a pickle round trip of a graph whose edges and degree views were already read, the copy's views belong to the copy (D.edges._graph is D and D.degree._graph is D) and follow later changes to it. An edges or degree view pickled on its own, including one taken from a temporary graph, unpickles into a view that still answers nbunch and weight calls (ev([1]), ev.data('w', nbunch=[1]), dv(weight='w'), dv(1)) and can be pickled again. While its graph is alive, a view's _graph is that graph. Graph.nbunch_iter keeps its behaviour and error messages. Add tests.
notes: networkx tuning task (October 4, 2026; user decision to add networkx as a tuning repository to find tasks where Sonnet 5.5 medium fails). Python 3.12 with no numpy/scipy: tests that need them are skipped, and none of the hidden tests do. networkx is not pip-installed in the benchmark venv, so its conftest warns about a "Mixed NetworkX configuration" (the nx_loopback test backend); results are the same on base and reference. Tuning only. Its suite is the whole networkx package (about 55 s), since the change is in the core graph classes.
